key_insight: At fixed friction stir welding settings, 1 g of graphite produced a more continuous AA7075–AZ31 weld region than 0 or 2 g, but substantial defects remained.
engineering_relevance: Graphite quantity may influence interfacial consolidation in dissimilar aluminium–magnesium welding, with excessive addition potentially disrupting bond formation.
method: Compared graphite interlayers of 0, 1 and 2 g between AA7075 and AZ31.
Used a square-profile HCHCr tool at 1000 rpm, 15 mm/min and 2 kN axial force.
Examined the 1 g weld using FESEM and EDS.
evidence_signal: The 0 and 2 g conditions lacked stable bonded regions; the 1 g condition showed improved continuity but retained discontinuities, void-like and crack-like features, and heterogeneous carbon distribution.
watch_item: This exploratory comparison at one processing condition does not establish an optimal graphite quantity or a universal weld-quality relationship.
paper_title: Effect of graphite interlayer quantity on weld formation and defect evolution in AA7075–AZ31 dissimilar friction stir welding
